samples.text:
In many cities today, more people are living in tall apartment buildings. There are some good points and bad points about this type of housing, but I think the advantages are bigger than the disadvantages.

The first reason is that high-rise buildings use land very efficient. Cities have a lot of people but not much space, so building upwards means that many families can live on a small piece of land. This can help to reduce the housing problem and keep the price of flats lower. Also, people who live in these buildings are usually close to the city centre, so they can go to work, school and shops easily and they do not need to drive a long distance every day. Many modern apartment blocks also have facilities like a gym, a swimming pool and security guards, which makes life more comfortable.

On the other hand, living in a high-rise building have some problems. For example, there is often no garden or green space, so children do not have a safe place to play outside. In addition, people in big buildings often do not know their neighbours, and some of them feel lonely and isolated. Another problem is safety. If there is a fire or the lift stop working, it can be very dangerous and difficult for old people to get out.

In conclusion, although high-rise apartments have some disadvantages such as the lack of green space and loneliness, I believe they are necessary for modern cities because they save land and are convenient. So in my opinion, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, especially if the government make sure the buildings are safe.

samples.text:
As urban populations continue to grow, high-rise apartment blocks have become the most common form of housing in many cities. Although this way of living has certain drawbacks, I believe the advantages are greater overall.

The main benefit of tall residential buildings is that they make efficient use of limited land. By housing hundreds of families on a single plot, they reduce the pressure to build on surrounding countryside and help to keep housing more affordable than it would otherwise be. Moreover, because high-rise blocks are usually located in central districts, residents can live close to their workplaces, schools and public transport. This not only saves time on commuting but also reduces the number of cars on the roads, which is better for environment. Many newer developments also provide shared facilities such as gyms, playgrounds and security staff that individual houses rarely have.

However, apartment living also has disadvantages. The most frequently mentioned is a weaker sense of community: residents may share a lift with dozens of people every day and yet hardly know any of them. Families with young children often complain about the lack of private outdoor space, while elderly residents can find themselves trapped if lifts break down. There are also concerns about safety in the event of fire, as evacuating a tall building is more difficult than leaving a house.

Nevertheless, most of these problems can be reduced through good design and regulation. Communal gardens, shared rooftop areas and strict fire-safety standards can make high-rise living both more sociable and more secure.

In conclusion, while tall apartment buildings can feel impersonal and present particular safety challenges, their efficient use of land and convenient locations make them an essential solution for crowded cities. For these reasons, I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · main ideas extended and supported, with a paragraph addressing the drawbacks · logical organisation and varied linking · good collocation · mostly error-free, one article slip.

samples.text:
Across the world's major cities, the skyline is increasingly dominated by residential towers, and a growing share of urban households now live many floors above the street. Although vertical living has undeniable shortcomings, I would argue that, in densely populated cities, its advantages prevail.

The strongest case for high-rise housing is a practical one. Land in city centres is scarce and expensive, and building upwards allows far more homes to be created on the same footprint than low-rise development ever could. This density has wider benefits: it limits urban sprawl into farmland and green belts, and it makes public transport, shops and services economically viable because enough people live within walking distance of them. For residents, the result is often a shorter commute and easier access to employment, education and leisure, which can significantly improve quality of life.

The drawbacks, however, are genuine. Tall buildings can be socially isolating, since the anonymity of long corridors and shared lifts rarely encourages the casual encounters that build neighbourly relationships. Families may struggle without private gardens, and older or disabled residents are particularly vulnerable when lifts fail. Safety is a further concern: evacuating hundreds of people from upper floors during a fire is inherently more complex than escaping from a house, and poorly maintained towers can become hazardous.

Yet these issues largely reflect how such buildings are designed and managed rather than the concept itself. Well-planned developments incorporate communal green spaces, community rooms and robust fire-safety systems, demonstrating that high-density living can be both safe and socially vibrant.

In conclusion, high-rise apartments may compromise privacy, outdoor space and, at times, community spirit, but these costs can be mitigated through thoughtful design. Given their efficient use of land and the accessibility they offer, I believe their advantages clearly outweigh their disadvantages.
samples.why: Well-developed, fully relevant response with a clear judgement · ideas logically sequenced and extended · skilful cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary (urban sprawl, footprint, economically viable) · wide range of error-free structures.
